DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.claim: Aflaha can mean becoming happy or blessed.
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.anchor: افلح سعد قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين قد افلح المؤمنون يعني سعدوا وقال تعالى في سورة سبح قد افلح من تزكى

DAMGHANI:v1p218/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r2.claim: Tazakkā can refer to paying the charity of the fast-breaking festival.

BURSEVI:v10p317/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p317/r7.claim: The successful escapes harm and gains what is hoped for by purifying from unbelief and sin through the reminder, or by growing in piety and fear.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r7.anchor: أي نجا من المكروه وظفر بما يرجوه

BURSEVI:v10p317/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p317/r8.claim: The word qad prepares listeners, after hearing about the fate of those who turn away, to hear the good outcome of those who remember.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r8.anchor: وكلمة قد لما أن عند ابار بسوء حال المتجنب عن الذكرى

BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.claim: The Imam orders the deeds as purifying false beliefs, recalling knowledge of God through His names and attributes, and serving through prayer and bodily obedience.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.anchor: قال الامام مراتب أعمال المكلف ثلاث فأولاها إزالة العقائد الفاسدة عن القلب

BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.claim: Another gloss says the purified person repents, hears the call to prayer, and goes out to pray; the next verse rebukes those who choose worldly work instead.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.anchor: ويقال قد أفلح من تزكى أي من تاب من الذنوب وذكر اسم ربه يعني إذا سمع الأذان خرج إلى الصلاة

QASHANI:87:13-15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:13-15/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:13-15/r2.claim: The successful person wins by cleansing the self’s qualities and the body’s darkness after attaining spiritual readiness.
QASHANI:87:13-15/r2.anchor: فاز وظفر من تطهر عن صفات نفسه وظلمات بدنه بعد حصول استعداده

SULAMI:v2p390#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p390#3/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p390#3/r1.claim: The successful person fears God in secret and in public.
SULAMI:v2p390#3/r1.anchor: قال سهل رحمه الله : فاز وسعد من اتقى الله في السر والعلانية

SULAMI:v2p390#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p390#3/r2.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v2p390#3/r2.claim: Success is purifying oneself from appetites, following whim, and the unruliness of one's temperament.
SULAMI:v2p390#3/r2.anchor: قال الجريري : افلح من طهر من شهوات نفسه ، ومتابعة هواه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says purification means turning away from idolatry.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : قد افلح من تزكى قال : من الشرك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r3.claim: Ikrima says the successful person is whoever says there is no deity but God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله : قد افلح من تزكى قال : من قال لا اله الا الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r4.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r4.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه قال : قد افلح من تزكى قال : من امن

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r5.claim: Ata also interprets purification as frequent seeking of forgiveness.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r5.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه قال : قد افلح من تزكى قال : من اكثر الاستغفار

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r6.claim: Qatada says purification is righteous action.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : قد افلح من تزكى قال : بعمل صالح

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.claim: A report explicitly graded weak says the Prophet commanded paying zakat al-fitr before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies the verse's purification with zakat al-fitr.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن كثير بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن عوف ، عن أبيه ، عن جده ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انه كان يامر بزكاة الفطر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r8.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r8.claim: Ata glosses purification as paying zakat al-fitr.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r8.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه : قد افلح من تزكى قال : ادى زكاة الفطر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.claim: Ibn Sirin says the person paid the fitr charity, then went out and prayed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه في قوله : قد افلح من تزكى قال : ادى صدقة الفطر ثم خرج فصلى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r10.claim: Asked if the verse concerns fitr, Ibn Abbas says he had not heard that interpretation; it concerns all zakat and, when pressed, all charities.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r10.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه قال : قلت لابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ارايت قوله : قد افلح من تزكى للفطر ! قال : لم اسمع بذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r11.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says purification means giving from one's wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r11.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قد افلح من تزكى يعني من ماله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r12.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r12.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r12.claim: Qatada says the purified person has pleased his Creator by giving from his wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r12.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قد افلح من تزكى قال : من ارضى خالقه من ماله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says a person who gives charity may pray two units and then recite this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.anchor: عن أبي الاحوص رضي الله عنه قال : لو ان الذي يتصدق بالصدقة صلى ركعتين ثم قرا قد افلح من تزكى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.claim: Ibn Masud says one setting out for prayer may give charity, linking the act with the verse's sequence of purification and prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : اذا خرج احدكم يريد الصلاة فلا عليه ان يتصدق بشئ لان الله يقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r6.claim: The reward passage is a rhetorical restart after the punishment, which was stated first as the main warning; the purified person is the same one who fears and remembers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r6.anchor: فالمراد ب { من تزكى } هنا عين المراد ب ( من يخشى ويذكر ) فقد عرف هنا بأنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r1.claim: Falah gathers success and benefit: attaining the good one seeks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r1.anchor: فإن الفلاح نجاح المرء فيما يطمح إليه فهو يجمع معنيي الفوز والنفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r2.claim: The past tense with qad presents success in the afterlife as certain, and encourages the wicked hearers to join those who feared and succeeded.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r2.anchor: والإتيان بفعل المضي في قوله أفلح } للتنبيه على المحقق وقوعه من الآخرة ، واقترانه بحرف { قد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r3.claim: Tazakkā means striving to become pure through self-purification; the tafaʿʿul form indicates effort, beginning with monotheism and good Islamic works, including almsgiving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r3.anchor: ومعنى { تزكى } : عالج أن يكون زكيا ، أي بذل استطاعته في تطهير نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet via Jabir explains purification as professing God's oneness, rejecting partners, and affirming the Prophet's mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.anchor: أخرج البزار عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من شهد أن لا إلاه إلا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.claim: Purification comes first because it is the foundation of the subsequent work: a cleansed soul receives guidance and turns more readily to good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.anchor: وقدم التزكي على ذكر الله والصلاة لأنه أصل العمل بذلك كله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.claim: The three qualities unfold in order: purifying false beliefs, recalling God's perfection with fear and hope, then obeying and worshipping; prayer represents worship and leads to other deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.anchor: وقد رتبت هذه الخصال الثلاث على الآية على ترتيب تولدها

TUSTARI:87:14/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:87:14/r1.claim: Success and felicity belong to one who fears God both privately and publicly.
TUSTARI:87:14/r1.anchor: قال: أي فاز وسعد من اتقى الله في السر والعلانية.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r1.claim: Aflaha means attaining one's desire; tazakka means purifying the self and cultivating it toward good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r1.anchor: أفلح في هذه الآية معناه: فاز ببغيته، وتزكى معناه: طهر نفسه ونماها إلى الخير.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets purification as saying there is no god but God, thereby cleansing oneself of idolatry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال لا إله إلا الله فتطهر من الشرك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the person whose deeds are pure is meant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: من كان عمله زاكيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r4.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Ahwas reads purification as giving some wealth away and purifying it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص: من رضخ من ماله وزكاه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains aflaha as finding permanent survival and success.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى قد أفلح قال الزجاج أي صادف البقاء الدائم والفوز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r2.claim: One view says the person purified himself from associating partners with God through faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r2.anchor: أحدها من تطهر [ من ] الشرك بالإيمان قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وعطاء وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation identifies purification with giving the ṣadaqat al-fiṭr; it is attributed to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Qatāda.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r3.anchor: والثاني من أعطى صدقة الفطر قاله أبو سعيد الخدري وعطاء وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r4.speaker: الحسن والربيع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r4.claim: A third view says the person whose deeds are sound and pure has succeeded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r4.anchor: والثالث من كان عمله زاكيا قاله الحسن والربيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r5.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r5.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ interprets it as all of the obligatory alms on wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r5.anchor: والرابع أنها زكوات الأموال كلها قاله أبو الأحوص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it means increasing through fear of God; zākī means growing and abundant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#3/r6.anchor: ومعنى الزاكي النامي الكثير قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.claim: The Ibn ʿAbbās interpretation is preferred for both verses: this sūra is Meccan by consensus, and there was no alms or Eid prayer in Mecca.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.anchor: والقول قول ابن عباس في الآيتين فإن هذه السورة مكية بلا خلاف ولم يكن بمكة زكاة ولا عيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r1.claim: The successful person purifies the soul of base traits and follows what God revealed to His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r1.anchor: أي: طهر نفسه من الأخلاق الرذيلة، وتابع ما أنزل الله على رسوله،

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r5.claim: Falāḥ, success, and gain are near-synonyms for attaining one’s goal.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r5.anchor: والفلاح والنجاح والغنم نظائر، وهو الظفر بالبغية

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.speaker: أبي العالية وأبي سعيد الخدري وابن عمر
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and Ibn ʿUmar connect purification with the alms of fast-breaking and the Eid prayer; Ibn ʿUmar would check that Nafiʿ had paid before leaving for prayer.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية، وأبي سعيد الخدري، وابن عمر

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.speaker: أبي ذر
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.claim: Abū Dharr asked the Prophet what the earlier scriptures contained; the Prophet answered by reciting these two verses.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.anchor: وعن أبي ذر، قلت: يا رسول الله، ما كان في الصحف الأولى؟

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.claim: Paradise is attained through the combined deeds named: purification consists of performing obligations and avoiding grave sins; purification, prayer, and remembrance are human actions.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.anchor: والتطهير إنما يحصل بأداء الواجبات واجتناب الكبائر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r1.claim: Tazakka may mean cleansing oneself of polytheism and sins, purifying oneself for prayer, increasing in piety, or giving charity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r1.anchor: أو تكثر من التقوى ، من الزكاة وهو النماء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r1.claim: He interprets purification as clearing oneself of idolatry through faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r1.anchor: من تطهر من الشرك بالإيمان , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r2.speaker: الحسن والربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r2.claim: They interpret it as righteous deeds becoming pure and growing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r3.speaker: أبو الأحوص
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r3.claim: He interprets the verse as referring to all obligatory wealth alms.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r3.anchor: زكاة الأموال كلها , قاله أبو الأحوص

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r4.claim: Another possible meaning is a person who increases in goodness and righteousness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r14.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r14.claim: He reports that the sura was revealed concerning Abu Bakr.

MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.claim: The successful person pays alms, bears witness that there is no god but God, and performs the five daily prayers.
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.anchor: قد أفلح من أدى الزكاة، وشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وصلى الصلوات الخمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#3/r1.claim: A successful person attains victory; “purifies himself” can mean becoming free of shirk, purifying oneself through prayer, or paying alms, by analogy with charity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ قد أفلح ﴾ نال الفوز ﴿ من تزكى ﴾ نطهر من الشرك

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r1.claim: Success is attaining Paradise by purifying oneself from shirk through faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r1.anchor: من تطهر من الشرك بإيمان قاله ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r2.speaker: الحسن والربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r2.claim: They interpret purification as one's deeds being wholesome and growing in reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن والربيع: من كان عمله زاكيا ناميا

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r3.claim: He explains purification as performing a righteous deed.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r3.anchor: وقال معمر عن قتادة: «تزكى» قام بعمل صالح

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r4.speaker: قتادة وعطاء وأبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r4.claim: They say the verse was revealed concerning the charity of breaking the fast.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r4.anchor: وعنه وعن عطاء وأبي العالية: نزلت في صدقة الفطر

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r10.speaker: أبو الأحوص وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r10.claim: They take purification to mean payment of all obligatory wealth zakat.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r10.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالآية زكاة الأموال كلها قاله أبو الأحوص وعطاء

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r11.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r11.claim: In Ibn Jurayj's report, Ata says the verse concerns all charitable giving, not only fitr charity.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r11.anchor: قلت لعطاء: { قد أفلح من تزكى } للفطر؟ قال: هي للصدقات كلها

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r12.claim: Another interpretation is purification of one's deeds from ostentation and shortcomings; the wording is apt because wealth is more often described with zakā than tazakkā.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r12.anchor: وقيل: هي زكاة الأعمال، لا زكاة الأموال

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r13.claim: A report from Jabir explains purification as confessing God's oneness, rejecting idols, and affirming Muhammad's messengership.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r13.anchor: وروى جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r14.claim: He glosses tazakkā as the confession that there is no god but God.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r14.anchor: وعن ابن عباس { تزكى } قال: لا إله إلا الله

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r15.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r15.claim: He reports its revelation about Uthman, who gave an orchard to replace a hypocrite's palm whose fallen dates fed an Ansari family; the hypocrite had refused the Prophet's offer of a palm in Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15/r15.anchor: وروى عنه عطاء قال: " نزلت في عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه

NAHHAS:v5p207/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p207/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa's report, says the one who purifies himself is purified from associating partners with God.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r1.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال من تزكى من الشرك أي تطهر

NAHHAS:v5p207/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r2.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p207/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the person who purifies himself is one whose deeds are virtuous.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن من تزكى من كان عمله زاكيا

NAHHAS:v5p207/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r3.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p207/r3.claim: Qatāda says the verse refers to one who pays his wealth's alms.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r3.anchor: والقول الآخر عن قتادة قال من تزكى أدى زكاة ماله

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.claim: The Prophet fulfills his duty by reminding; people then diverge in response and outcome, and God deals with them according to how they receive the reminder.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.anchor: فإذا نهض [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] بهذا العبء فقد أدى ما عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:87:14/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:14/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:14/r1.claim: Success and salvation lie on the other side of wretchedness, through purification and remembrance; tazakki means cleansing oneself of every stain and defilement.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:14/r1.anchor: والتزكي : التطهر من كل رجس ودنس

QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r3.claim: One who purifies, remembers, and prays certainly prospers: in this life through a living connection and the sweetness of remembrance, and in the next through escape from Hell and attaining bliss and approval.

RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r1.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself from the previously mentioned disbelief, since the verse does not name another object of purification.
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r1.anchor: لما لم يذكر في الآية ما يجب التزكي عنه علمنا أن المراد هو التزكي عما مر ذكره

RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, purification means increasing in piety, since zakā carries the sense of growth; 23:1–2 and 2:5 associate success with gathered virtues.
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r2.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج : تكثر من التقوى لأن معنى الزاكي النامي الكثير

RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r3.claim: The unrestricted word refers to its fullest sense: purifying the heart from disbelief’s darkness is the highest purification.
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r3.anchor: الاسم المطلق ينصرف إلى المسمى الكامل ، وأكمل أنواع التزكية هو تزكية القلب عن ظلمة الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses purification as declaring that there is no deity but God.
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#3/r4.anchor: بما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال معنى : { تزكى } قول : لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.claim: That Eid interpretation faces the Qur’an’s usual order of prayer before alms and the sura’s Meccan setting, where neither Eid nor fitra existed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.anchor: أن عادة الله تعالى في القرآن تقديم ذكر الصلاة على ذكر الزكاة

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi answers that God may praise people in advance for practices He knows will occur later.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.anchor: لا يمتنع أن يقال : لما كان في معلوم الله تعالى أن ذلك سيكون أثنى على من فعل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.claim: Muqatil reads the first phrase as giving alms and the second as affirming oneness in prayer; unlike the Eid view, this concerns obligatory alms and prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل : { قد أفلح من تزكى } ( الأعلى : 14 ) أي تصدق من ماله

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r7.claim: Another view takes purification as cleansing deeds of ostentation and shortcomings, not paying wealth-alms; the wording fits deeds, as 35:18 says.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r7.anchor: ليس المراد منه زكاة المال بل زكاة الأعمال أي من تطهر في أعماله من الرياء والتقصير

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r1.claim: One interpretation is that purification means escaping idolatry by professing God's Oneness.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r1.anchor: According to some, He indeed prospers who is purified refers to purification from idolatry by professing God’s Oneness

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r2.claim: Another interpretation is purification through good deeds.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r2.anchor: Others say that it refers to purification through good deeds

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r3.speaker: still others
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r3.claim: A further interpretation identifies purification with the alms given for ʿĪd al-fiṭr.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r3.anchor: still others say it refers specifically to the alms given on ʿĪd al-fiṭr

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.speaker: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.claim: The sixth Imam says the verse order refers to alms being given in the morning before the two cycles of the ʿĪd prayer.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.anchor: the sixth Imam, Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq, stated that the order of the verses refers to the alms being given in the morning

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.claim: Read together, the verses describe whole-person worship: purifying the heart, remembering God with the tongue, and performing God's commands, especially prayer.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.anchor: These two verses can be taken together as referring to worshipping with all aspects of one’s being

TAB:87:14/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:14/r1.claim: The successful person purifies himself from disbelief and sin, obeys God's commands, and performs the obligations God imposed.
TAB:87:14/r1.anchor: قد نجح وأدرك طلبته من تطهّر من الكفر ومعاصي الله ،   وعمل بما أمره الله به ،   فأدّى فرائضه .

TAB:87:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:87:14/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets purification as cleansing oneself of association with God.
TAB:87:14/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّى يقول :  من تَزَكّى من الشرك .

TAB:87:14/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB:87:14/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verse describes someone whose deeds are righteous.
TAB:87:14/r3.anchor: عن الحسن ،   في قوله قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّى قال :  من كان عمله زاكيا .

TAB:87:14/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:14/r4.claim: Qatāda explains purification as acting with scrupulous piety.
TAB:87:14/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّى قال :  يعمل وَرِعا .

TAB:87:14/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r5.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:87:14/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says the purified person is one who declares that there is no god but God.
TAB:87:14/r5.anchor: عن عكرِمة ،   في قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّى من قال :  لا إله إلاّ الله .

TAB:87:14/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:14/r6.claim: Another group interprets the verse as referring to payment of the alms due on one's property.
TAB:87:14/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون :  بل معنى ذلك :  قد أفلح من أدّى زكاة ماله .

TAB:87:14/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r7.speaker: أبو الأحوص
TAB:87:14/r7.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ urges a person able to give a small charity to do so before praying.
TAB:87:14/r7.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّى قال :  من استطاع أن يرضَخَ فليفعل ،   ثم ليقم فليصلّ .

TAB:87:14/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r8.speaker: أبو الأحوص
TAB:87:14/r8.claim: He says a worshipper approached by a petitioner should give his zakat before prayer.
TAB:87:14/r8.anchor: إذا أتى أحدكم سائل وهو يريد الصلاة ،   فليقدّم بين يدي صلاته زكاته ،   فإن الله يقول

TAB:87:14/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:14/r9.claim: Qatāda also describes a man as purifying himself of his wealth and pleasing his Creator.
TAB:87:14/r9.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّى تزكى رجل من ماله ،   وأرضى خالقه .

TAB:87:14/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r10.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB:87:14/r10.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya connects the verse with the pre-Eid alms: he asks whether the narrator sent his zakat, then says that was why he had asked.
TAB:87:14/r10.anchor: دخلت على أبي العالية ،   فقال لي :  إذا غدوت غدا إلى العيد فمرّ بي ،   قال :  فمررت به

TAB:87:14/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:14/r11.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB:87:14/r11.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the people of Medina consider no charity better than this alms and providing water.
TAB:87:14/r11.anchor: وقال :  إن أهل المدينة لا يَرَون صدقة أفضل منها ،   ومن سِقاية الماء .

TAB:87:19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r6.speaker: author
TAB:87:19/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the demonstrative covers the nearby verses about purification, prayer, preferring this life, and the better, lasting afterlife, since this is the nearest referent; ṣuḥuf means the books of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:19/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ،   قول من قال :  إن قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكى وَذَكَرَ اسمَ رَبّهِ فَصَلّى

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets purification as being cleansed of associating partners with God.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {قد أفلح من تزكى} [الأعلى: 14] يقول: من تزكى من الشرك "

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the successful person as one whose deeds are righteous.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله " {قد أفلح من تزكى} [الأعلى: 14] قال: من كان عمله زاكيا "

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r3.claim: Qatāda explains purification as acting with scrupulous piety.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، " {قد أفلح من تزكى} [الأعلى: 14] قال: يعمل ورعا "

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r4.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the purified person as one who says there is no deity but God.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: " {قد أفلح من تزكى} [الأعلى: 14] من قال: لا إله إلا الله "

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r5.claim: Others take the verse to mean that a person has paid the obligatory alms from his wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: قد أفلح من أدى زكاة ماله

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r6.speaker: أبو الأحوص
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ urges anyone able to give charity to do so before standing to pray.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص، " {قد أفلح من تزكى} [الأعلى: 14] قال: من استطاع أن يرضخ فليفعل

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r7.claim: Qatāda says a man purified part of his wealth and pleased his Creator.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {قد أفلح من تزكى} [الأعلى: 14] تزكى رجل من ماله، وأرضى خالقه "

TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r8.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya applies the verse to the alms given for breaking the fast, reporting that Medina’s people considered it among the best charities.
TAB-FULL:v24p318#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي خلدة، قال: دخلت على أبي العالية، فقال لي: إذا غدوت غدا إلى العيد

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.claim: Ṭabarī prefers that “this” refers to the nearest preceding lines, 87:14–17, because a demonstrative most naturally points to what is nearby; ṣuḥuf means books or scrolls.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.anchor: وإنما قلت: ذلك أولى بالصحة من غيره، لأن هذا إشارة إلى حاضر، فلأن يكون إشارة إلى ما قرب منها

TABATABAI:87:14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14/r1.claim: The opening of the sūra is Meccan, but its closing verses about purification, alms, and Eid prayer were revealed in Medina after those practices were legislated; reports calling the whole sūra Meccan can refer to its opening.
TABATABAI:87:14/r1.anchor: وسياق الآيات في صدر السورة سياق مكي وأما ذيلها أعني قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى } الخ

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r10.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself of worldly attachments that divert from the afterlife; turning to God and spending in His path cleanse attachment to earth and wealth.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r10.anchor: التزكي هو التطهر والمراد به التطهر من ألواث التعلقات الدنيوية الصارفة عن الآخرة

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r11.claim: Ritual ablution illustrates cleansing the traces of what faces, hands, and feet have done.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r11.anchor: حتى أن وضوء الصلاة تمثيل للتطهر عما كسبته الوجوه والأيدي والأقدام

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.claim: Although the verses read generally, reports from the Imams and Sunni transmitters identify them with alms of breaking the fast and Eid prayer.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.anchor: والآيتان بحسب ظاهر مدلولهما على العموم لكن ورد في المأثور عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أنهما نزلتا في زكاة الفطر وصلاة العيد

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.claim: Al-Ṣādiq explains purification as paying alms of breaking the fast and the prayer as going to the prayer ground for Eid prayer; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes parallel reports, including an abbreviated one from al-Qummī.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.anchor: وفي الفقيه وسئل الصادق عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وحل { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال قال من أخرج الفطرة

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that the Prophet would recite these verses and distribute fitra before going to the Eid prayer-ground; similar reports are attributed to several early authorities and to the Prophet through ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول { قد أفلح من تزكى

TABATABAI:87:19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:19/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:87:19/r1.claim: In a report from Abū Dharr, the Prophet answers whether revelation contains anything from Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls by reciting 87:14–19, supporting the author’s broader referent for “this.”
TABATABAI:87:19/r1.anchor: عن أبي ذر في حديث قلت يا رسول الله فما في الدنيا مما أنزل الله عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى؟ قال يا أبا ذر اقرأ

ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r1.claim: Aflaha means attaining lasting life and bliss; tazakkā means growing through God-consciousness, and zakī means growing and abundant.
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r1.anchor: أي قد صادف البقاء الدائم والفوز بالنعيم.

TABRISI:87:10-17/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r8.speaker: عطاء، عكرمة
TABRISI:87:10-17/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrima take purification as leaving idolatry and professing that there is no god but God.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r8.anchor: تطهر من الشرك وقال لا إله إلا الله عن عطاء وعكرمة

TABRISI:87:10-17/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، قتادة
TABRISI:87:10-17/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda interpret success as becoming righteous through good deeds and scrupulous piety.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r9.anchor: صار زاكيا بالأعمال الصالحة والورع عن ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة

THALABI:v10p184#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r1.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p184#3/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima, and reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explain purification as leaving idolatry and confessing that there is no god but God.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r1.anchor: أي تطهر من الشرك وقال: لا إله إلا الله، هذا قول عطاء وعكرمة ورواية الوالي عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v10p184#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p184#3/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the successful person has deeds that are pure.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: من كان عمله زاكيا

THALABI:v10p184#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p184#3/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the successful person as one who did righteous deeds and practiced scrupulous piety.

THALABI:v10p184#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r4.speaker: أبو الأحوص
THALABI:v10p184#3/r4.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ says he gave some of his property and paid its alms.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r4.anchor: وعن أبو الأحوص: رضح من ماله وأدى زكاة ماله

THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd prayed for the person who gives charity, then prays, and recited these verses.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود يقول: رحم الله امرءا تصدق ثم صلى ثم يقرأ هذه الآية

THALABI:v10p184#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r6.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v10p184#3/r6.claim: Others identify purification as the alms of breaking the fast; Abū Hārūn reports this from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: هو صدقة الفطر، وروى أبو هارون عن أبي سعيد الخدري

THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says the person gives the alms of breaking the fast, goes out for Eid, and prays.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.anchor:
قال:
أعطى صدقة الفطر.
وذكر اسم ربه فصلى قال: خرج إلى العيد فصلى

THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar waited for confirmation that the charity had been sent before leaving for the Eid prayer ground; the author reports this as the occasion of the verse.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.anchor: كان ابن عمر إذا صلى الغداة- يعني من يوم العيد- قال: يا نافع أخرجت الصدقة

THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya checked that the visitor had washed and dispatched his alms before Eid prayer, then said the people of Medina know no better charity than that and providing water.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.anchor: إن أهل المدينة لا يرون صدقة أفضل منها ومن سقاية الماء

THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.claim: A prophetic report explains purification as paying the alms of breaking the fast and going out to the prayer ground to pray.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: قد أفلح من تزكى قال: «أخرج زكاة الفطر

THALABI:v10p185/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p185/r1.claim: The author questions the Eid and fitra interpretation because the sura is Meccan by consensus, before there was an Eid or fitra alms in Mecca.
THALABI:v10p185/r1.anchor: قلت: ولا أدري ما وجه هذا التأويل، لأن هذه السورة مكية بالإجماع ولم يكن بمكة عيد

THALABI:v10p185/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r3.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v10p185/r3.claim: A report from Jābir interprets purification as professing God's oneness, abandoning idols, and affirming the Prophet; prayer is the five prayers, maintained at the call and their appointed times.
THALABI:v10p185/r3.anchor:
قال: «من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله وخلع الأنداد وشهد أني رسول
الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r10.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r10.claim: The successful person is Uthman ibn Affan; “purifies himself” means professes that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r10.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد # عثمان بن عفان (¬1). ومعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r13.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r13.claim: The successful person has pure deeds and performs righteous acts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن: أفلح من كان عمله زاكيا (¬1)، وعمل صالحا (¬2)، وهو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r14.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r14.claim: Purification means growth through reverence for God; “pure” can mean growing and abundant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r14.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى تزكى تكثر بتقوى الله، ومعنى الزاكي:

WAHIDI-QT:87:14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:14/r1.claim: The successful person attains lasting residence in Paradise.
WAHIDI-QT:87:14/r1.anchor: { قد أفلح } صادف البقاء في الجنة

WAHIDI-QT:87:14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:14/r2.claim: The one purified is someone who does much righteous work.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r10.claim: The successful person attains lasting residence in Paradise by doing more righteous deeds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r10.anchor: قد أفلح } صادف البقاء في الجنة { من تزكى } أكثر من العمل الصالح.

ELMALILI:87:14-15/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r1.claim: Success means escaping evil and attaining one's aim; purification includes taking admonition, cleansing the heart of shirk and bad character, and the body of physical and spiritual impurity.

ELMALILI:87:14-15/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r2.claim: Purification also includes faith, sincerity, ritual washing and ablution, and giving zakat to seek standing purified before God.
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r2.anchor: bedenini maddî ve mânevî pisliklerden temizleyip iman ve ihlâs ve gusül ve abdest ile paklanan ve zekâtını verip huzûr-ı ilâhîde temize çıkmak için çalışan

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:14:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:14:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:14:anmerkung/r1.claim: For the meaning of prospering through purification, the note directs readers to Q 91:9.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza again addresses the messenger: he first praises God, perhaps with close followers, then speaks to a wider audience with an admonition that makes verse 6’s revelation public in purpose.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz beginnt wie das erste mit einem Aufruf an den Verkünder

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.claim: Verses 10–11 contrast good and bad responses to proclamation; verse 11 expands the bad response with a conventional warning of Hell, balanced by the promise to the good in verses 14–15.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.anchor: Auf den das zweite Gesätz einleitenden Aufruf folgt in V. 10.11 eine Antithese

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.claim: The passage forms a chiasm: the responses of good and bad in verses 10–11 correspond to their fates in verses 12–15, as in Q 92:5–11 and 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.anchor: Zusammen mit der an den Guten gerichteten Verheißung V. 14.15 ergibt sich eine chiastische Struktur

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.claim: The warning’s implied content includes fear of God, continued purification, invocation of God’s name, and prayer; verse 15 reprises verse 1’s call to recall the Creator’s favors.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.anchor: Erwähnt werden ständiges Bemühen um „Läuterung“ sowie Anrufung des Namens Gottes und Gebet

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.claim: Calls to the messenger can make a general appeal, with the messenger exemplary for each believer, as Robinson argues.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r9.claim: Although social ethics are not explicit as in Q 90 and Q 107, they are probably implied by purification.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r9.anchor: Sozialethische Aspekte, wie sie in anderen Suren prominent sind

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.claim: Those who heed admonition, cleanse hearts of shirk, sin, and bad character, purify themselves through prayer and charity, and remember God attain salvation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.anchor: öğütlere kulak veren, kalplerini şirk, günah ve kötü ahlâkın kirlerinden temizleyen, namaz kılıp sadaka ve zekât vermek suretiyle nefsini arındıran kimselerin kurtuluşa erecekleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r8.claim: Tezekka can mean self-discipline and avoiding shirk, evil, and sin through faith and obedience, or purification by giving zakat; in these early Meccan passages zakat means general financial duties, not the later formal institution (51:19; 70:24; 9:103).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r8.anchor: âyetteki tezekkâ kelimesi hem malı haramlardan ve kul haklarından hem de nefsi günah kirlerinden arındırmayı ifade eder

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib interprets purification as the alms of the fast-breaking festival.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r1.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن أمية عن سعيد بن المسيب في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى ﴾ قال زكاة الفطر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r2.claim: Qatāda interprets purification as righteous action.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى ﴾ بعمل صالح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r1.claim: Success means escaping what is feared and attaining what one hopes for.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r1.anchor: قد أفلح أي نجا من المكروه وظفر بما يرجوه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others explain purification as abandoning shirk through recollection and taking admonition from the reminder.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r2.anchor: من تزكى أي تطهر من الشرك بتذكره واتعاظه بالذكرى وحمله على ذلك مزوي عن ابن عباس وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r3.claim: A report from Jābir, raised to the Prophet, glosses this as testifying that none is God but God, rejecting rivals, and affirming the Messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r3.anchor: وأخرج البزار وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال في ذلك من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r4.claim: Some interpreters include purification from both disbelief and sin, allowing the preceding mention to abbreviate the most important part.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r4.anchor: واعتبر بعضهم أمرين فقال أي تطهر من الكفر والمعصية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r5.claim: Another gloss derives tazakkā from growth and reads it as increasing in piety and fear of God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r5.anchor: وقيل تزكى أي تكثر من التقوى والخشية من الزكاء وهو النماء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r6.claim: Other explanations are preparing oneself for prayer or giving alms; the latter is reported from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, Qatāda, and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109/r6.anchor: وقيل تظهر للصلاة وقيل آتى الزكاة وروي هذا عن أبي الأحوص وقتادة وجماعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r2.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r2.claim: Ata, Ikrima, and reports from Ibn Abbas and Saʿid b. Jubayr say the successful person purifies himself from idolatry and professes that there is no god but God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r2.anchor: تطهر من الشرك وقال: لا إله إلا الله. هذا قول عطاء وعكرمة، ورواية الوالبي وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the successful person is one whose deeds are righteous.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: من كان عمله زاكيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r4.claim: Another interpretation is alms at the end of Ramadan; Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports that ‘he purified himself’ means paying the fitr charity.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.claim: Nafiʿ reports that Ibn Umar checked whether charity had been given before going to the prayer ground, connecting the verses to charity and Eid prayer; Abu al-Aliya and Ibn Sirin hold this view.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.anchor: وروى نافع: كان ابن عمر إذا صلى الغداة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.claim: Some object that the surah is Meccan, before Eid or fitr charity existed; al-Baghawi replies that revelation can precede the ruling, as with the Prophet’s lawful entry into Mecca and the prophecy of Badr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.anchor: يجوز أن يكون النزول سابقا على الحكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r2.claim: The person who succeeds purifies himself of unbelief and sin, increases in piety, prepares for prayer, or pays the alms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r2.anchor: تطهر من الكفر والمعصية، أو تكثر من التقوى من الزكاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes تزكى as giving the fitr alms, remembering God as the Eid takbīr, and prayer as the Eid prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.anchor: وقيل { تزكى } تصدق للفطر { وذكر اسم ربه } كبره يوم العيد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r3.claim: True purification combines abandoning prohibitions and pursuing commands through disciplined worship and struggle after the warning against ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r3.anchor: فجمع الاجتناب والاجتلاب بالتزكية بالتبتل بالأبواب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r4.claim: Prosperity means attaining every desired good; purification cleanses belief, character, speech, deeds, and wealth while growing inward and outward acts and charity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r4.anchor: تطهيرها من فاسد الاعتقادات والأخلاق والأقوال والأفعال والأموال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.claim: Purification is the glorification commanded at the sura's opening and the good actions that follow from it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.anchor: وذلك هو التسبيخ الذي أمر به أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.claim: The purification, remembrance, and prayer reprise the opening's divine traits: removing defects and acquiring perfections; this paired ellipsis links prayer with escape from the greatest fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.anchor: وكان متخلقا بما ذكر من أخلاق الله في أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.claim: The wording can include fitr almsgiving, Eid takbirs, and Eid prayer despite the sura being Meccan, since wording is general and revelation may precede a ruling.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.anchor: والآية صالحة لإرادة زكاة الفطر وتكبيرات العيد وصلاته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.speaker: الرازي في اللوامع
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.claim: Al-Razi says fitr almsgiving precedes Eid prayer; Ibn Masud recited this verse after saying may God show mercy to one who gives charity then prays.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وتقدم زكاة الفطر على صلاة العيد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.claim: Ibn Masud linked the verse to giving charity and then praying, although the sura is Meccan and the ruling came later.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول : رحم الله أمرأ تصدق ثم صلى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.claim: Ibn Umar instructed Nafi to act similarly and said the verse was revealed about this practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.anchor: وزاد البغوي أن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان يأمر نافعا رضي الله عنه بنحو ما قال ابن مسعود

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.claim: Al-Bazzar reports from Awf ibn Malik that the Prophet ordered fitr almsgiving before Eid prayer and recited this verse; the chain's Kathir ibn Abd Allah was judged hasan by al-Tirmidhi but weakened by others.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.anchor: وروى البزار : ( عن عوف بن مالك الأشجعي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.claim: Ending with purification returns to the beginning's glorification and soul-cleansing; God does not leave creation without guidance or create them purposelessly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.anchor: وكان في إتيانه والتذكير به إعلام بأن الله تعالى لم يهمل الخلق

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r1.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r1.anchor: قال: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من آمن

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r2.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ also interprets purification as frequent seeking of forgiveness.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r2.anchor: قال: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من أكثر الاستغفار

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets purification as performing righteous deeds.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r3.anchor: في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: بعمل صالح

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.claim: A weak-chain report says the Prophet ordered the fiṭra alms before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies the verse with fiṭra.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر قبل أن يصلي صلاة العيد

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.claim: The Prophet recited these verses and distributed the fiṭra alms before going to the Eid prayer ground.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.claim: He explains purification as giving fiṭra before setting out for Eid, and remembering God and praying as going out and performing the prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: أعطى صدقة الفطر قبل أن يخرج إلى العيد

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd identifies purification here as fiṭra alms.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: زكاة الفطر

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar would give fiṭra as he set out and recite the two verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عمر كان يقدم صدقة الفطر حين يغدو ثم يغدو وهو يتلو

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says these verses were revealed about giving fiṭra before the Eid prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في إخراج صدقة الفطر قبل صلاة العيد

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r10.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r10.claim: Wāthila interprets purification as scattering wheat at the prayer ground before the Eid prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r10.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} الآية قال: إلقاء القمح قبل الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the verses were revealed about fiṭra: one gives the alms, then prays.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى} قال: نزلت في صدقة الفطر

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya checked whether a visitor had eaten and sent his zakāt; he says Medina considered no charity better than fiṭra and providing water.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.anchor: عن أبي خلدة رضي الله عنه قال: دخلت على أبي العالية فقال لي إذا غدوت غدا إلى العيد فمر بي

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r3.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets purification as paying fiṭra.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r3.anchor: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: أدى زكاة الفطر

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.claim: Ibn Sīrīn says one pays fiṭra and then goes out to pray.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: أدى صدقة الفطر ثم خرج فصلى

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī urges paying the zakāt as early as possible on Eid and cites these verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي رضي الله عنه قال: قدم الزكاة ما استطعت يوم الفطر ثم قرأ

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r6.claim: Asked whether purification meant fiṭra, Ibn ʿAbbās said he had not heard that and understood it as all zakāt, then all forms of charity.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r6.anchor: قال: قلت لابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أرأيت قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} للفطر قال: لم أسمع بذلك

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr interprets purification as purification of one’s wealth.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه {قد أفلح من تزكى} يعني من ماله

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r8.claim: Qatāda distinguishes purification of wealth from purification of character.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r8.anchor: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: تزكى رجل من ماله وتزكى رجل من خلقه

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ urges anyone able to give charity before prayer to do so, citing the verse; another wording suggests praying two units after giving.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه قال: رحم الله امرأ تصدق ثم صلى ثم قرأ {قد أفلح من تزكى}

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a person setting out for prayer may give charity, citing these verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.anchor: أبي الأحوص عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: إذا خرج أحدكم يريد الصلاة فلا عليه أن يتصدق بشيء

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r1.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r1.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ interprets purification as giving a small charitable gift.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r1.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من رضخ

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.claim: Asked whether the Prophet received anything from those scrolls, he recited the passage from purification and prayer through the superiority of the afterlife and the scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.anchor: هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال: يا أبا ذر نعم {قد أفلح من تزكى

ITQAN:v2p338#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r1.claim: Suyuti glosses “purifies himself” as being free of polytheism.

ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet’s gloss: purification is testifying to God’s oneness, rejecting idols, and testifying to his messengership; remembering God and praying refers to keeping up the five prayers.
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.anchor: أخرج البزار عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى ﴾ ( من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله وخلع الأنداد

ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r1.claim: Aflaha means to succeed and attain one’s desired end; tazakkā means to purify oneself.
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r1.anchor: { قد أفلح } : أي فاز وظفر بالبغية ، { من تزكى } : تطهر .

ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses purification as being cleansed of idolatry and professing that there is no god but God.
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : من الشرك ، وقال : لا إله إلا الله .

ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the successful person is one whose deeds are pure.
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن : من كان عمله زاكياً .

ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r4.speaker: أبو الأحوص وقتادة وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r4.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, Qatāda, and others understand it as giving from one’s wealth and purifying it.
ABUHAYYAN:87:14/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص وقتادة وجماعة : من رضخ من ماله وزكاه .

ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.claim: The meaning is that remembering God leads to belief; the verse says the successful person performs both worship and charity.
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.anchor: والمعنى : أنه لما تذكر آمن بالله ، ثم أخبر عنه تعالى أنه أفلح من أتى بهاتين العبادتين الصلاة والزكاة

ALUSI:87:14/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:14/r1.claim: Aflaha means being saved from what one fears and attaining what one hopes for.
ALUSI:87:14/r1.anchor: أي نجا من المكروه وظفر بما يرجوه

ALUSI:87:14/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:14/r2.claim: The initial interpretation of tazakkā is purification from associating partners with God through remembrance and taking admonition from the reminder.
ALUSI:87:14/r2.anchor: أي تطهر من الشرك بتذكره واتعاظه بالذكرى وحمله على ذلك مروي عن ابن عباس وغيره

ALUSI:87:14/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:87:14/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others are reported to explain purification here as cleansing oneself of shirk through remembrance and admonition.
ALUSI:87:14/r3.anchor: وحمله على ذلك مروي عن ابن عباس وغيره

ALUSI:87:14/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI:87:14/r4.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports that the Prophet explained it as testifying that none is god but God, rejecting idols, and bearing witness that he is God’s messenger.
ALUSI:87:14/r4.anchor: وأخرج البزار وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

ALUSI:87:14/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:87:14/r5.claim: Some say tazakkā means purifying oneself from disbelief and disobedience; the earlier view may simply emphasize the most important part.
ALUSI:87:14/r5.anchor: واعتبر بعضهم أمرين فقال أي تطهر من الكفر والمعصية وعليه يجوز أن يكون ما تقدم من باب الاقتصار على الأهم

ALUSI:87:14/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:14/r6.claim: Another view derives tazakkā from growth and takes it to mean increasing in piety and reverent fear.
ALUSI:87:14/r6.anchor: وقيل تزكى أي تكثر من التقوى والخشية من الزكاء وهو النما

ALUSI:87:14/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:14/r7.claim: Another interpretation is purification in preparation for prayer.

ALUSI:87:14/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:14/r8.speaker: أبو الأحوص وقتادة
ALUSI:87:14/r8.claim: A further interpretation takes the phrase as giving alms; this is transmitted from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, Qatāda, and others.
ALUSI:87:14/r8.anchor: وقيل آتي الزكاة وروى هذا عن أبي الأحوص وقتادة وجماعة

ALUSI:87:15/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r21.claim: Qad anticipates good news about the rememberer after mention of the rejecter's bad afterlife; the clause answers the implied question about the rememberer's fate.
ALUSI:87:15/r21.anchor: لما أنه عند الاخبار بسوء حال المتجنب عن الذكر في الآخرة يتوقع السامع

ALUSI:87:15/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r22.claim: Expected wording would be successful is the one who remembers, but the text substitutes the purifier clause to describe the rememberer by his traits.
ALUSI:87:15/r22.anchor: وكان الظاهر قد أفلح من تذكر إلا أنه وضع من تزكى إلى آخره موضع من تذكر

ALUSI:91:11/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r15.speaker: صاحب الانتصاف
ALUSI:91:11/r15.claim: The author of al-Intiṣāf prefers taking God as the subject of purification because the pronouns in the preceding oaths then consistently refer to God and because 87:14, with ‘purified’ as a passive-like result, fits that reading.
ALUSI:91:11/r15.anchor: ورجحه صاحب الانتصاف بأن الضمائر في { والسماء وما بناها } [ الشمس : 5 ]

BAGHAWI:87:14/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:14/r1.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة
BAGHAWI:87:14/r1.claim: ʿAta and ʿIkrima, along with al-Walibi and Saʿid ibn Jubayr reporting from Ibn ʿAbbas, say the successful person purifies himself from idolatry and declares there is no god but God.
BAGHAWI:87:14/r1.anchor: تطهر من الشرك وقال : لا إله إلا الله . هذا قول عطاء وعكرمة ، ورواية الوالبي وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس .

BAGHAWI:87:14/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:14/r2.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:87:14/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the successful person is one whose deeds are pure.
BAGHAWI:87:14/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن : من كان عمله زاكياً .

BAGHAWI:87:14/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:14/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI:87:14/r3.claim: Another view takes the purification as the alms of breaking the fast; Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports this interpretation as giving zakat al-fitr.
BAGHAWI:87:14/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : هو صدقة الفطر ، روي عن أبي سعيد الخدري في قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : أعطى صدقة الفطر .

BAYDAWI:87:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:14/r1.claim: Purification may mean cleansing oneself from unbelief and sin.

BAYDAWI:87:14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:14/r2.claim: The verb may mean increasing in piety, by association with the sense of growth in zakāh.
BAYDAWI:87:14/r2.anchor: أو تكثر من التقوى من الزكاة

BAYDAWI:87:14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:14/r3.claim: Another interpretation is purification for prayer.

BAYDAWI:87:14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:14/r4.claim: It may refer to paying the obligatory alms.

BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.claim: A ritual interpretation links purification to alms at the end of Ramadan, remembrance to the Eid takbīr, and prayer to the Eid prayer.
BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.anchor: وقيل تزكى تصدق للفطر وذكر اسم ربه كبره يوم العيد فصلى صلاته

BIQAI:87:12/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:12/r4.claim: The verses use interwoven omission: fear, the fruit of happiness, implies its omitted opposite hardness, while the misery named as a cause implies omitted happiness; this encourages the first and warns against the second.
BIQAI:87:12/r4.anchor: وهي الخشية دليلاً على حذف ضدها من الثاني

BIQAI:87:12/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r5.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI:87:12/r5.claim: Al-Malawī explains the Qurʾān's concision: one passage gives a consequence without its cause, another the cause without its consequence, and each implies the other, as do decree, ordainment, and judgment.
BIQAI:87:12/r5.anchor: قال الملوي : ولا شك أن القرآن العظيم على أحسن ما يكون

BIQAI:87:14/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:14/r1.claim: The earlier punishment follows from failing to purify oneself, since the person was not disposed to fear; the argument now turns to religious duties of avoiding evil and pursuing good.
BIQAI:87:14/r1.anchor: فكان التقدير : لأنه لم يزك نفسه

BIQAI:87:14/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:14/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:14/r2.claim: Purification means cleansing beliefs, character, speech, deeds, and wealth of corruption, while cultivating inward and outward acts and giving charity.
BIQAI:87:14/r2.anchor: أعمل نفسه في تطهيرها من فاسد الاعتقادات والأخلاق والأقوال والأفعال والأموال

BIQAI:87:14/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:14/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:14/r3.claim: Purification gathers obedience and avoidance of prohibitions through devotion and spiritual striving; it is the commanded glorification at the sūra's opening and its consequences.
BIQAI:87:14/r3.anchor: فجمع الاجتناب والاجتلاب بالتزكية بالتبتل بالأبواب والملازمة للأعتاب بامتثال الأمر واجتناب النهي

BIQAI:87:14/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:14/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:14/r4.claim: Aflaha means that the person who purifies himself wins every desired good and becomes the happiest.
BIQAI:87:14/r4.anchor: أي أعمل نفسه في تطهيرها من فاسد الاعتقادات والأخلاق

BIQAI:87:14/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:14/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:14/r5.claim: The person succeeds by connecting to God, following the unimpeachable exemplar, and keeping to the sound path so that every moment is filled with worship and not lost to heedlessness.
BIQAI:87:14/r5.anchor: والاقتداء بمن لا يزيغ من الارتباط بطريقة مثلى

BIQAI:87:15/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r5.claim: Purification, remembrance, and prayer remove self-admiration and its faults, strip away defects, and acquire perfections modeled on the sūra's opening; the passage also evokes stages of medical treatment.
BIQAI:87:15/r5.anchor: وكان متخلقاً بما ذكر من أخلاق الله في أول السورة من التخلي عن النقائص بالتزكية

BIQAI:87:15/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r7.claim: A second interwoven omission links the fire mentioned first with its omitted opposite in the next verse, and the purification named next with its omitted opposite earlier; purification, remembrance, and prayer figure in a therapy sequence.
BIQAI:87:15/r7.anchor: من الاحتباك في الاحتباك : ذكر أولاً الصلى دليلاً على حذف

BIQAI:87:15/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r8.claim: The general wording can include zakāt al-fiṭr, the Eid takbīrs, and Eid prayer even though the sūra is Meccan and fasting was prescribed in Medina; revelation may precede a ruling.
BIQAI:87:15/r8.anchor: والآية صالحة لإرادة زكاة الفطر وتكبيرات العيد وصلاته وإن كانت السورة مكية

BIQAI:87:15/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r9.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI:87:15/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī in al-Lawāmiʿ says zakāt al-fiṭr precedes Eid prayer and cites Ibn Masʿūd's prayer for the giver of charity before reciting this verse.
BIQAI:87:15/r9.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وتقدم زكاة الفطر على صلاة العيد

BIQAI:87:15/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI:87:15/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd prayed for mercy on whoever gave charity and then prayed, and then recited this verse.
BIQAI:87:15/r10.anchor: ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول : رحم الله امرأً تصدق ثم صلى

BIQAI:87:15/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI:87:15/r11.claim: Al-Baghawī reports that Ibn ʿUmar told Nāfiʿ to do likewise and said the verse was revealed concerning this practice.
BIQAI:87:15/r11.anchor: أن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان يأمر نافعاً رضي الله عنه بنحو ما قال ابن مسعود

BIQAI:87:15/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:87:15/r12.claim: Al-Bazzār reports from ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī that the Prophet ordered zakāt al-fiṭr before Eid prayer and recited this verse.
BIQAI:87:15/r12.anchor: عن عوف بن مالك الأشجعي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر قبل أن يصلي صلاة العيد

BIQAI:87:15/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r13.speaker: الترمذي
BIQAI:87:15/r13.claim: The report's chain includes Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, whom al-Tirmidhī graded ḥasan while other critics weakened him.
BIQAI:87:15/r13.anchor: وفي السند كثير بن عبد الله - حسّن له الترمذي وضعفه غيره

DURR:87:14/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:14/r1.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet explaining purification as affirming God’s oneness, rejecting idols, and testifying to his messengership; remembrance and prayer mean five prayers observed carefully and on time.
DURR:87:14/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:14/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:14/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses purification as freedom from shirk, remembrance as affirming God’s oneness, and prayer as five daily prayers.
DURR:87:14/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله

DURR:87:14/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:87:14/r3.claim: ʿIkrima glosses purification as saying “There is no god but God.”
DURR:87:14/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله :

DURR:87:14/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:14/r4.claim: Through ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās likewise glosses purification as saying “There is no god but God.”
DURR:87:14/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله

DURR:87:14/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r5.speaker: عطاء
DURR:87:14/r5.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه قال : { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من آمن .

DURR:87:14/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r6.speaker: عطاء
DURR:87:14/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ also says purification means frequent seeking of forgiveness.
DURR:87:14/r6.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه قال : { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من أكثر الاستغفار .

DURR:87:14/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:14/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses purification as performing righteous deeds.
DURR:87:14/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله :

DURR:87:14/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:14/r8.claim: A weak report says the Prophet ordered fiṭr charity before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies the verse as fiṭr charity.
DURR:87:14/r8.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن كثير بن عبدالله بن عمرو بن عوف عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر قبل أن يصلي صلاة العيد

DURR:87:14/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:14/r9.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet recited the verses and distributed fiṭr charity before Eid prayer.
DURR:87:14/r9.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR:87:14/r10.claim: Abū Saʿīd interprets purification as paying fiṭr charity before Eid; remembrance and prayer mean going out to Eid and praying.
DURR:87:14/r10.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : أعطى صدقة الفطر قبل أن يخرج إلى العيد

DURR:87:14/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR:87:14/r11.claim: Abū Saʿīd glosses purification as zakāt al-fiṭr.
DURR:87:14/r11.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
