DURR:87:14/r12.claim: Qatāda reports that ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar paid fiṭr charity before Eid, reciting the verses.
DURR:87:14/r12.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه أن عبدالله بن عمر كان يقدم صدقة الفطر حين يغدو ثم يغدو وهو يتلو { قد أفلح من تزكى

DURR:87:14/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r13.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR:87:14/r13.claim: Nāfiʿ reports Ibn ʿUmar’s view that these verses were revealed about paying fiṭr charity before Eid prayer.
DURR:87:14/r13.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال : إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في إخراج صدقة الفطر قبل صلاة العيد

DURR:87:14/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r14.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
DURR:87:14/r14.claim: Wāthila interprets purification as giving grain before Eid prayer at the prayer ground.
DURR:87:14/r14.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r15.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:14/r15.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the verses were revealed about fiṭr charity: purify, then pray.
DURR:87:14/r15.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r16.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:14/r16.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya asked a visitor before Eid whether he had eaten and sent charity; he cited the verses and praised fiṭr charity and providing water.
DURR:87:14/r16.anchor: عن أبي خلدة رضي الله عنه قال : دخلت على أبي العالية

DURR:87:14/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r17.speaker: عطاء
DURR:87:14/r17.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says purification is paying zakāt al-fiṭr.
DURR:87:14/r17.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : أدى زكاة الفطر .

DURR:87:14/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r18.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR:87:14/r18.claim: Muḥammad b. Sīrīn says the person paid fiṭr charity, then went out and prayed.
DURR:87:14/r18.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r19.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR:87:14/r19.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī advised paying charity as early as possible on Eid, citing the verses.
DURR:87:14/r19.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي رضي الله عنه قال : قدم الزكاة ما استطعت يوم الفطر ثم قرأ { قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى }

DURR:87:14/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:14/r20.claim: Asked whether purification meant fiṭr charity, Ibn ʿAbbās said he had not heard that; he meant all zakāt and all charities.
DURR:87:14/r20.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه قال : قلت لابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

DURR:87:14/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r21.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:87:14/r21.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr glosses purification as giving from one’s wealth.
DURR:87:14/r21.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه { قد أفلح من تزكى } يعني من ماله .

DURR:87:14/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r22.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:14/r22.claim: Qatāda says purification means pleasing one’s Creator through wealth.
DURR:87:14/r22.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من أرضى خالقه من ماله .

DURR:87:14/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r23.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:14/r23.claim: Qatāda gives further possibilities: purification through wealth or character.
DURR:87:14/r23.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من أرضى خالقه من ماله .

DURR:87:14/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r24.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:14/r24.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ urged charity before prayer; one wording says do so if able, another says give, pray, and recite the verse.
DURR:87:14/r24.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه قال : رحم الله امرئ تصدق ثم صلى ثم قرأ { قد أفلح من تزكى } الآية

DURR:87:14/r25.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r25.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:87:14/r25.claim: Through Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, Ibn Masʿūd says one setting out for prayer may give charity, citing the verses.
DURR:87:14/r25.anchor: من طريق أبي الأحوص عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : إذا خرج أحدكم يريد الصلاة فلا عليه أن يتصدق بشيء

DURR:87:14/r26.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r26.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:14/r26.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ also says a donor should pray two rakʿas and recite the verse.
DURR:87:14/r26.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه قال : لو أن الذي تصدق بالصدقة صلى ركعتين ثم قرأ { قد أفلح من تزكى } الآية

DURR:87:14/r27.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r27.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:14/r27.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ glosses purification as giving a small amount.
DURR:87:14/r27.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من رضخ .

DURR:87:15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r1.speaker: النبي
DURR:87:15/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet glossing purification as affirming God's oneness, renouncing idols, and testifying to his messengerhood; remembrance and prayer mean the five prayers kept at their times.
DURR:87:15/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:15/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:15/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses purification as freedom from shirk, remembrance as affirming God's oneness, and prayer as the five daily prayers.
DURR:87:15/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

DURR:87:15/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:87:15/r3.claim: Ikrima says the successful person is one who professes there is no god but God.

DURR:87:15/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r5.speaker: عطاء
DURR:87:15/r5.claim: In another gloss, Ata says purification means frequent seeking of forgiveness.

DURR:87:15/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:15/r6.claim: Qatada interprets purification as performing righteous deeds.

DURR:87:15/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r7.speaker: النبي
DURR:87:15/r7.claim: A report through Kathir ibn Abd Allah, whose chain al-Suyuti calls weak, says the Prophet directed fitr alms before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies purification as fitr alms.
DURR:87:15/r7.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن كثير بن عبدالله بن عمرو بن عوف عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:15/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r8.speaker: النبي
DURR:87:15/r8.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that the Prophet recited these verses and distributed fitr alms before setting out for the Eid prayer ground.
DURR:87:15/r8.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR:87:15/r9.claim: Abu Sa'id interprets purification as paying fitr alms before leaving for Eid and the following phrase as going out to pray.
DURR:87:15/r9.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR:87:15/r10.claim: Qatada reports that Ibn Umar would pay fitr alms when departing in the morning, then leave while reciting these verses.
DURR:87:15/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه أن عبدالله بن عمر كان يقدم صدقة الفطر

DURR:87:15/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR:87:15/r11.claim: Ibn Umar says the verses were revealed concerning payment of fitr alms before the Eid prayer.
DURR:87:15/r11.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r12.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
DURR:87:15/r12.claim: Wathila glosses purification as putting out grain at the Eid prayer ground before the prayer.
DURR:87:15/r12.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع رضي الله عنه في قوله

DURR:87:15/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r13.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:15/r13.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the verses were revealed about fitr alms: purify first, then pray.
DURR:87:15/r13.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه في قوله

DURR:87:15/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r14.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:15/r14.claim: Abu Khilda recounts that Abu al-Aliya asked whether he had paid his alms before Eid, then said Medinans knew no better charity than fitr alms and providing water.
DURR:87:15/r14.anchor: عن أبي خلدة رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r15.speaker: عطاء
DURR:87:15/r15.claim: Ata identifies purification here as paying fitr alms.

DURR:87:15/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r16.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR:87:15/r16.claim: Ibn Sirin says the successful person pays fitr alms, then goes out and prays.
DURR:87:15/r16.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه في قوله

DURR:87:15/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r17.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR:87:15/r17.claim: Al-Nakha'i advises paying the fitr alms as early as possible on Eid, then cites the verses.
DURR:87:15/r17.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:15/r18.claim: Asked whether purification specifically means fitr alms, Ibn Abbas says he had not heard that; he meant zakat and charities generally.

DURR:87:15/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r19.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:87:15/r19.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses purification as purification of one's wealth.
DURR:87:15/r19.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r20.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:15/r20.claim: Qatada says purification means using one's wealth to please the Creator.
DURR:87:15/r20.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله

DURR:87:15/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r21.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:15/r21.claim: Qatada also distinguishes a person purifying his wealth from one purifying his character.

DURR:87:15/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r22.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:15/r22.claim: Abu al-Ahwas urges giving charity before praying, citing the verse; one wording says whoever can give charity before prayer should do so.
DURR:87:15/r22.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r23.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:15/r23.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says a person who gives charity should pray two cycles and then recite the verse.
DURR:87:15/r23.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r24.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:87:15/r24.claim: Abu al-Ahwas transmits Ibn Mas'ud's view that one leaving for prayer may give some charity, based on these verses.
DURR:87:15/r24.anchor: أبي الأحوص عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r25.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r25.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:15/r25.claim: Abu al-Ahwas glosses purification as giving a small amount of charity.
DURR:87:15/r25.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه

IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.claim: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas say verses 14–15 came down about Eid prayer and alms at the end of Ramadan, making those verses Medinan and the sura partly Makkan and partly Medinan.
IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عمر وابن عباس أن قوله تعالى { قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } نزل في صلاة العيد وصدقة الفطر

IBNASHUR:87:14/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r1.claim: This explanatory resumption resolves the audience’s expectation after mention of those who fear and the most wretched: the warning and their punishment come first, then the promised reward.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r1.anchor: استئناف بياني لأن ذكر { من يخشى } [ الأعلى : 10 ] وذكر { الأشقى } [ الأعلى : 11 ] يثير استشراف السامع لمعرفة أثر ذلك

IBNASHUR:87:14/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r2.claim: The one who purifies himself is the same person who fears and remembers; remembering God’s name identifies him, and remembering is the aim of the reminder commanded in verse 9.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r2.anchor: فالمراد ب { من تزكى } هنا عين المراد ب « من يخشى ويذكر » فقد عرف هنا بأنه الذي ذكر اسم ربه

IBNASHUR:87:14/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r3.claim: Falah means succeeding in one’s aims and includes both winning and benefit: attaining the good one seeks.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r3.anchor: فإن الفلاح نجاح المرء فيما يطمح إليه فهو يجمع معنيي الفوز والنفع

IBNASHUR:87:14/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r4.claim: The perfect-tense aflaha and particle qad present afterlife success as certain, as in 23:1 and 91:9.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r4.anchor: والإتيان بفعل المضي في قوله أفلح } للتنبيه على المحقق وقوعه من الآخرة ، واقترانه بحرف { قد } لتحقيقه

IBNASHUR:87:14/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r5.claim: Addressing the warning’s rejecters with this assurance stirs them to join those who feared and succeeded.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r5.anchor: لأن الكلام موجه إلى الأشقين الذين تجنبوا الذكرى إثارة لهمتهم في الالتحاق بالذين خشوا فأفلحوا

IBNASHUR:87:14/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r6.claim: Tazakka means working to become pure and exerting oneself to purify the soul, as in the contrast between purification and corruption at 91:9–10.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r6.anchor: ومعنى { تزكى } : عالج أن يكون زكياً ، أي بذل استطاعته في تطهير نفسه وتزكيتها

IBNASHUR:87:14/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r7.claim: The tafaʿʿala form conveys effort and deliberate striving.

IBNASHUR:87:14/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r8.claim: Purification begins with tawhid and readiness for the good works taught by Islam, including alms on wealth.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r8.anchor: وأصل ذلك هو التوحيدُ والاستعداد للأعمال الصالحة التي جاء بها الإسلام ويجيء بها ، فيشمل زكاة الأموال

IBNASHUR:87:14/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r9.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNASHUR:87:14/r9.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits from the Prophet, through Jabir, that purification means confessing God’s oneness, disavowing idols, and affirming the Prophet’s mission; Ibn Ashur gives no grading for this report.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r9.anchor: أخرج البزار عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : { قد أفلح من تزكى }

IBNASHUR:87:14/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:14/r11.claim: Purification precedes remembrance and prayer because it grounds those acts: a purified soul receives guidance, recognizes its benefits, and increasingly turns toward them; here purification is by faith.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r11.anchor: وقدم التزكي على ذكر الله والصلاة لأنه أصل العمل بذلك كله فإنه إذا تطهرت النفس أشرقت فيها أنوار الهداية

IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.claim: The three qualities follow their natural order: remove false beliefs and corrupt thoughts, know God’s perfect qualities and wisdom so as to fear and hope, then turn to obedience and worship.
IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.anchor: وقد رتبت هذه الخصال الثلاث على الآية على ترتيب تولدها . فأصلها : إزالة الخباثة النفسية من عقائد باطلة

IBNATIYYA:87:14/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r1.claim: Aflaha means to attain one's aim; tazakkā means to purify the self and cultivate it toward good.
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r1.anchor: في هذه الآية معناه : فاز ببغيته ،

IBNATIYYA:87:14/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person professes “There is no god but God” and is purified of associating partners with God.
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : قال لا إله إلا الله فتطهر من الشرك

IBNATIYYA:87:14/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r3.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the phrase as having righteous deeds.
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن : من كان عمله زاكياً

IBNATIYYA:87:14/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r4.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNATIYYA:87:14/r4.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says it describes someone who gives a portion of his wealth and purifies it through almsgiving.

IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر وابن المسيب
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.claim: They apply the verses to Eid al-Fitr: giving zakat al-fitr, remembering God on the way to the prayer ground until the imam appears, and performing the Eid prayer.
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر وابن المسيب : هذه الآية في صبيحة يوم الفطر فتزكى ، أدى زكاة الفطر

IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.claim: A report from Abu Sa'id says the Prophet recited this verse and distributed the fitra before setting out for the Eid prayer.
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.speaker: قتادة وكثير من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.claim: Qatada and many interpreters take tazakkā as paying wealth-zakat and ṣallā as performing the five daily prayers.
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة وكثير من المتأولين : { تزكى } : أدى زكاة ماله ، و «صلى » معناه صلى الخمس

IBNKATHIR:87:14/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:14/r1.claim: The successful person purifies the self of base traits and follows what God revealed to His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR:87:14/r1.anchor: طهَّر نفسه من الأخلاق الرذيلة ، وتابع ما أنزل الله على رسوله

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.claim: A report from Jābir interprets purification as bearing witness that none is god but God, rejecting idols, and affirming Muhammad’s messengership; prayer means the five prayers observed carefully. Al-Bazzār says this is its only route from Jābir.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى } قال : " من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya applied the verse to giving zakāt al-fiṭr before Eid prayer; he says Medinans regarded it, along with providing water, as the best charity.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.anchor: حدثنا مروان بن معاوية ، عن أبي خلدة قال : دخلت على أبي العالية فقال لي

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to order people to give the charity of breaking the fast and recite this verse.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.anchor: روينا عن أمير المؤمنين عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه كان يأمر الناس بإخراج صدقة الفطر

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ says a person approached by a supplicant before prayer should give his zakāt before praying, applying this verse.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص : إذا أتى أحدكم سائل وهو يريد الصلاة ، فليقدم بين يدي صلاته زكاته

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses the verse as purifying one’s wealth and pleasing one’s Creator.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى } زكى ماله وأرضى خالقه

KASHSHAF:87:14/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:14/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:14/r1.claim: Tazakkā means purifying oneself from associating partners with God and from sins.
KASHSHAF:87:14/r1.anchor: تطهر من الشرك والمعاصي .   أو تطهر للصلاة

KASHSHAF:87:14/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:14/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:14/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the person purifies himself for prayer.
KASHSHAF:87:14/r2.anchor: أو تطهر للصلاة .   أو تكثر من التقوى

KASHSHAF:87:14/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:14/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:14/r3.claim: The word can also mean increasing in piety, from zakā meaning growth.
KASHSHAF:87:14/r3.anchor: أو تكثر من التقوى ،   من الزكاة وهو النماء

KASHSHAF:87:14/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:14/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:14/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means performing zakāh, just as tasaddaqa means giving charity.
KASHSHAF:87:14/r4.anchor: أو تفعل من الزكاة ،   كتصدق من الصدقة

MAWARDI:87:14/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:14/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:87:14/r1.claim: The successful person is one who purifies himself of idolatry through faith.
MAWARDI:87:14/r1.anchor: من تطهّر من الشرك بالإيمان ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:87:14/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:14/r2.speaker: الحسن والربيع
MAWARDI:87:14/r2.claim: The successful person has righteous deeds that are pure and growing.
MAWARDI:87:14/r2.anchor: من كان صالح عمله زكياً نامياً ،   قاله الحسن والربيع

MAWARDI:87:14/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:14/r3.speaker: أبو الأحوص
MAWARDI:87:14/r3.claim: The phrase refers to paying all the obligatory alms on one's wealth.
MAWARDI:87:14/r3.anchor: أنه عنى زكاة الأموال كلها ،   قاله أبو الأحوص

MAWARDI:87:14/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:14/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:14/r4.claim: Māwardī also allows that it means someone who increases in goodness and righteousness.
MAWARDI:87:14/r4.anchor: ويحتمل خامساً : أنه من ازداد خيراً وصلاحاً .

MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.claim: Muqatil cites the description of one who purifies himself, remembers God, and prays from al-A'la as a contrast: the Meccan unbelievers do not purify themselves or pray.
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.anchor:
قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى
[الأعلى: 14، 15] يقول الله تعالى في هذه السورة { كلا بل } لا تزكون، ولا تصلون

NASAFI:87:14/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:14/r1.claim: Aflaha means that the person attained success.
NASAFI:87:14/r1.anchor: { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } نال الفوز { مَن تزكى }

NASAFI:87:14/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:14/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:14/r2.claim: Tazakka can mean cleansing oneself from idolatry, purifying oneself for prayer, or paying zakat; its form is analogous to tasaddaqa from sadaqa.
NASAFI:87:14/r2.anchor: { من تزكى } تطهر من الشرك أو تطهر للصلاة أو أدى الزكاة

QURTUBI:87:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة
QURTUBI:87:14/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, and Ikrima say the successful person gains lasting residence in Paradise by cleansing himself of idolatry through faith.
QURTUBI:87:14/r1.anchor: أي قد صادف البقاء في الجنة ، أي من تطهر من الشرك بإيمان . قاله ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة

QURTUBI:87:14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r2.speaker: الحسن والربيع
QURTUBI:87:14/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Rabi say the verse describes someone whose deeds are pure and growing.
QURTUBI:87:14/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن والربيع : من كان عمله زاكيا ناميا

QURTUBI:87:14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:87:14/r3.claim: Qatada explains tazakka as doing righteous deeds; Ma'mar transmits the explanation.
QURTUBI:87:14/r3.anchor: قال معمر عن قتادة : " تزكى " قال بعمل صالح

QURTUBI:87:14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r4.speaker: قتادة وعطاء وأبو العالية
QURTUBI:87:14/r4.claim: Qatada, Ata, and Abu al-Aliya say the verse was revealed about the end-of-Ramadan alms.
QURTUBI:87:14/r4.anchor: وعنه وعن عطاء وأبي العالية : نزلت في صدقة الفطر

QURTUBI:87:14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r5.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI:87:14/r5.claim: Ibn Sirin says the person paid the alms and then went out and prayed.
QURTUBI:87:14/r5.anchor: وعن ابن سيرين " قد أفلح من تزكى . وذكر اسم ربه فصلى " قال : خرج فصلى بعدما أدى

QURTUBI:87:14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r6.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI:87:14/r6.claim: Ikrima says a man would say “I advance my alms before my prayer”; Sufyan cites the verse in connection with that practice.
QURTUBI:87:14/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة : كان الرجل يقول أقدم زكاتي بين يدي صلاتي . فقال سفيان

QURTUBI:87:14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر
QURTUBI:87:14/r7.claim: Abu Sa'id and Ibn Umar identify purification as fitr alms and prayer as Eid prayer; Abu al-Aliya agrees and mentions Medina's regard for charity and providing water.
QURTUBI:87:14/r7.anchor: وروي عن أبي سعيد الخدري وابن عمر : أن ذلك في صدقة الفطر ، وصلاة العيد . وكذلك قال أبو العالية

QURTUBI:87:14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:14/r8.claim: A report transmitted by Kathir ibn Abd Allah from his father and grandfather identifies tazakka as paying fitr alms and prayer as Eid prayer; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI:87:14/r8.anchor: وروى كثير بن عبد الله عن أبيه عن جده ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى : " قد أفلح من تزكى " قال

QURTUBI:87:14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
QURTUBI:87:14/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say the worshipper remembers God on the way to the prayer ground, then performs Eid prayer.
QURTUBI:87:14/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك : " وذكر اسم ربه " في طريق المصلى

QURTUBI:87:14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r10.speaker: أبو الأحوص وعطاء
QURTUBI:87:14/r10.claim: Abu al-Ahwas and Ata say the verse concerns all obligatory wealth alms, not only Ramadan fitr alms.
QURTUBI:87:14/r10.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالآية زكاة الأموال كلها . قاله أبو الأحوص وعطاء

QURTUBI:87:14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r11.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI:87:14/r11.claim: When Ibn Jurayj asked whether this referred only to fitr alms, Ata replied it concerns all charitable alms.
QURTUBI:87:14/r11.anchor: قلت لعطاء : " قد أفلح من تزكى " للفطر ؟ قال : هي للصدقات كلها

QURTUBI:87:14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:14/r12.claim: Another view means cleansing deeds of ostentation and shortcomings rather than paying wealth alms; Arabic more often says wealth was purified than a person purified himself.
QURTUBI:87:14/r12.anchor: وقيل : هي زكاة الأعمال ، لا زكاة الأموال

QURTUBI:87:14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:14/r13.claim: Jabir ibn Abd Allah reports the Prophet's interpretation as testifying that none is worthy of worship but God, renouncing rivals, and witnessing Muhammad as messenger; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI:87:14/r13.anchor: وروى جابر بن عبد الله قال : قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:87:14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:14/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas gives “there is no god but God” as the meaning of tazakka.
QURTUBI:87:14/r14.anchor: وعن ابن عباس " تزكى " قال : لا إله إلا الله

QURTUBI:87:14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r15.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:14/r15.claim: A report through Ata from Ibn Abbas says 87:14 concerns Uthman, who replaced a hypocrite's leaning date tree with an orchard after the Prophet's offer of a tree in Paradise was refused; 87:11 concerns the hypocrite. No grading is stated.
QURTUBI:87:14/r15.anchor: وروى عنه عطاء قال : نزلت في عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه . قال : كان بالمدينة منافق كانت له نخلة

QURTUBI:87:14/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r16.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:87:14/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.
QURTUBI:87:14/r16.anchor: وذكر الضحاك أنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI:87:14/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:14/r17.claim: Al-Qurtubi refers to his treatment of fitr alms in al-Baqara, but notes that the majority call this sura Meccan, when Mecca had neither Eid nor fitr alms.
QURTUBI:87:14/r17.anchor: وقد تقدم أن هذه السورة مكية ، في قول الجمهور ، ولم يكن بمكة عيد ولا زكاة فطر

QURTUBI:87:14/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:14/r18.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI:87:14/r18.claim: Al-Qushayri says it could praise people who comply with a future command concerning fitr alms and Eid prayer.
QURTUBI:87:14/r18.anchor: القشيري : ولا يبعد أن يكون أثنى على من يمتثل أمره

RAZI:87:14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:14/r1.claim: One reading connects the promise to the preceding warning: success belongs to the person who purifies himself from the stain of unbelief.
RAZI:87:14/r1.anchor: لما ذكر وعيد من أعرض عن النظر والتأمل

RAZI:87:14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:14/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI:87:14/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the phrase means increasing in piety, since the root sense of “pure” includes growing and becoming abundant.
RAZI:87:14/r2.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج : تكثر من التقوى

RAZI:87:14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:14/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:14/r3.claim: The growth-in-piety interpretation is supported by the declaration of success for believers characterized by humility in prayer.
RAZI:87:14/r3.anchor: قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

RAZI:87:14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:14/r4.claim: It is also supported by the opening description of the God-conscious as successful.

RAZI:87:14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:14/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:14/r5.claim: Rāzī favors purification from unbelief because the verse does not name what to purify from, so the earlier context supplies it.
RAZI:87:14/r5.anchor: لما لم يذكر في الآية ما يجب التزكي عنه علمنا أن المراد هو التزكي عما مر ذكره قبل الآية

RAZI:87:14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:14/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:14/r6.claim: He adds that an unrestricted term denotes its fullest instance, and the fullest purification is removing unbelief’s darkness from the heart.
RAZI:87:14/r6.anchor: وأكمل أنواع التزكية هو تزكية القلب عن ظلمة الكفر فوجب صرف هذا المطلق إليه

RAZI:87:14/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:14/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:87:14/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “purifies himself” as saying, “There is no god but God.”
RAZI:87:14/r7.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال معنى : { تزكى } قول :

RAZI:87:15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's reading and organizes religious action into purifying belief, knowing God, and serving Him.
RAZI:87:15/r2.anchor: وأقول : هذا التفسير متعين وذلك لأن مراتب أعمال المكلف ثلاثة

RAZI:87:15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r3.claim: The first stage, removing false beliefs from the heart, is what the preceding verse calls purification.
RAZI:87:15/r3.anchor: فالمرتبة الأولى : هي المراد بالتزكية في قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى }

RAZI:87:15/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r7.speaker: عكرمة وأبو العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر
RAZI:87:15/r7.claim: These authorities read the passage as giving alms before going to the Eid prayer, then praying Eid with the imam.
RAZI:87:15/r7.anchor: وهذا قول عكرمة وأبي العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر

RAZI:87:15/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:87:15/r8.claim: The Eid-alms and Eid-prayer interpretation is also narrated as a report raised to the Prophet; al-Rāzī states no grading.
RAZI:87:15/r8.anchor: وروي ذلك مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI:87:15/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that the Eid reading puts alms before prayer, whereas the Qurʾān customarily mentions prayer before zakat.
RAZI:87:15/r9.anchor: أن عادة الله تعالى في القرآن تقديم ذكر الصلاة على ذكر الزكاة لا تقديم الزكاة على الصلاة

RAZI:87:15/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r10.speaker: الثعلبي
RAZI:87:15/r10.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī says the sūra is Meccan by consensus, when neither Eid nor zakat al-fiṭr existed in Mecca; al-Rāzī uses this as an objection.
RAZI:87:15/r10.anchor: قال الثعلبي : هذه السورة مكية بالإجماع ولم يكن بمكة عيد ولا زكاة فطر

RAZI:87:15/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r11.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:87:15/r11.claim: Al-Wāḥidī replies that God may praise people for a practice He knows will occur later.
RAZI:87:15/r11.anchor: أجاب الواحدي عنه بأنه لا يمتنع أن يقال

RAZI:87:15/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r12.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:87:15/r12.claim: Muqātil reads purification as giving from one's wealth and remembering God through affirming His oneness in prayer.
RAZI:87:15/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل : { قد أفلح من تزكى } أي تصدق من ماله وذكر ربه بالتوحيد في الصلاة

RAZI:87:15/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r13.claim: Unlike the Eid interpretation, Muqātil's reading concerns the obligatory alms and prayers.
RAZI:87:15/r13.anchor: والفرق بين هذا الوجه وما قبله أن هذا يتناول الزكاة والصلاة المفروضتين

RAZI:87:15/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r14.claim: Another reading takes purification as cleansing one's deeds of ostentation and deficiency, rather than paying zakat on wealth; ordinary usage says wealth is zakā, not tazakkā.
RAZI:87:15/r14.anchor: ليس المراد منه زكاة المال بل زكاة الأعمال أي من تطهر في أعماله من الرياء والتقصير

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r21.claim: Success belongs to one purified from sins, faults, and fixation on creatures, who pays alms and wins salvation.

FARRA:v3p256/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r12.claim: Success through purification means doing good and giving charity; another view specifies charity before Eid prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.claim: The fortunate attain success by purification, remembering their Lord, and prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.anchor: Glad tidings of success are given to the fortunate who

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r4.claim: Those who benefited from the Prophet's reminders purify themselves from polytheism and disbelief and receive success and God's pleasure in both lives.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r5.claim: Aḥlaḥa means to win and obtain one's desire, and tazakkā means to purify oneself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r5.anchor: قد أفلح: أي فاز وظفر بالبغية، من تزكى: تطهر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets purification as leaving associationism and professing there is no god but God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: من الشرك، وقال: لا إله إلا الله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes purification to mean that a person's deeds are sound and pure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: من كان عمله زاكيا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r8.speaker: أبو الأحوص وقتادة وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r8.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, Qatāda, and others say the person gives some wealth and purifies it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص وقتادة وجماعة: من رضخ من ماله وزكاه.

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.claim: The Prophet glosses purification as affirming God's oneness, rejecting idols, and testifying that he is God's Messenger; prayer is the five prayers observed at their times.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى}

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.claim: Purification means freedom from associating partners; remembrance means affirming God's oneness; prayer means the five daily prayers.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من الشرك

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r10.claim: Ikrima says the successful person is one who says there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من قال لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, via Ikrima, likewise interprets purification as saying there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r11.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى}
